title: Library loans and due dates
instructions:
Build an in-memory library loan tracker with explicit calendar dates.

## Files
- `loans.py`: implement `parse_date` and `LoanTracker`.

`parse_date(text: str) -> datetime.date` accepts only a valid calendar date
in exactly YYYY-MM-DD form (ASCII digits, four-digit year). Invalid types,
formats, or dates raise ValueError. Dates and intervals use calendar days.

`LoanTracker()` starts empty. Book and borrower identifiers must be strings
nonempty after stripping surrounding whitespace, otherwise ValueError; store
and look up the stripped identifiers. The public methods are:
- `checkout(book: str, borrower: str, on: str, days: int = 14) -> str`:
  record a loan due parse_date(on) + days and return its ISO date string.
  days must be a positive int excluding bool (ValueError otherwise).
  An already-loaned book raises ValueError.
- `return_book(book: str) -> str`: remove its loan and return its borrower;
  an unknown book raises KeyError.
- `renew(book: str, on: str, days: int = 7) -> str`: extend the EXISTING due
  date by days, returning the new ISO due date. Reject renewal when on is
  later than the old due date (ValueError); renewal on the due date is valid.
  Validate days like checkout; unknown book raises KeyError.
- `loans() -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]`: (book, borrower, ISO due date)
  tuples sorted by book, in a fresh list.
- `overdue(on: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]`: loans whose due date is
  strictly before on, sorted by (due date, book), in a fresh list.

All rejected mutations leave the tracker unchanged. Inputs will not cause
date arithmetic to exceed datetime.date's range. No persistence is required.
